title: Decision of the AI Office
summary: The AI Office has issued a decision outlining its stance on AI governance and the principles for responsible AI deployment. The decision provides guidance for organizations on compliance, transparency, and ethical considerations related to AI.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Technology Specialists in AI
summary: The policy announces a vacancy for a technology specialist in AI at the organization’s office, outlining the role’s purpose and scope. It sets out the required qualifications, responsibilities, and application procedures for prospective candidates.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Lead Scientific Adviser
summary: The document announces a vacancy for the position of Lead Scientific Adviser in the AI Office, outlining the role’s responsibilities and the desired qualifications. It invites qualified candidates to apply in order to guide the organization’s AI research strategy and policy development.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Legal Officers
summary: The policy outlines how an AI office will fill a vacancy for a legal officer, detailing the qualifications, responsibilities, and selection process for the role. It emphasizes the importance of legal oversight in AI initiatives, ensuring compliance with applicable laws and regulations.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Policy Officers
summary: This policy outlines procedures for filling vacancies in AI-related offices, detailing the roles and responsibilities of the policy officers who will manage AI governance. It specifies how positions will be advertised, evaluated, and assigned to ensure consistent and qualified oversight of AI initiatives.

title: AI Act Scientific Panel
summary: The AI Act Scientific Panel is a group of experts assembled to review and provide scientific guidance on the proposed AI Act, ensuring the legislation is informed by current research and technical best practices. They evaluate technical aspects, risk assessment frameworks, and ethical implications to help shape effective AI governance policies.

title: Draft Standardisation Request
summary: This document proposes the creation of standardized guidelines or procedures for a specific area. It is a draft request aimed at establishing consistent practices to improve reliability, safety, and interoperability.

title: CoP Consultation Notice
summary: This notice announces a consultation on establishing or revising a Community of Practice (CoP). It invites stakeholders to share their views on the CoP’s goals, structure, and how it will be implemented.

title: CoP Call for Expression of Interest
summary: This document is a call for expressions of interest to establish a community of practice focused on AI. It invites participants to propose projects, share expertise, and collaborate on developing best practices and resources in the field.

title: CoP Graphic: Overview of Iterative Drafting Process
summary: This graphic outlines the iterative drafting process used by the Community of Practice. It shows the main stages—from initial drafting through review, feedback, and revision—to illustrate how documents evolve over multiple cycles.

title: CoP Graphic: Timeline of Drafting Process
summary: The document shows a visual timeline that outlines the key stages and milestones of the AI policy drafting process. It indicates when each phase began and ended, and highlights the final approval point.

title: Code of Practice: 1st Draft
summary: This document outlines the first draft of a code of practice for AI, detailing guidelines and standards to promote responsible AI development and use. It serves as a framework for organizations to align their AI activities with best practices and ethical considerations.

title: Code of Practice: 2nd Draft
summary: This document outlines guidelines for responsible AI use and development. It provides best practices, standards, and compliance requirements for organizations.

title: Code of Practice: 3rd Draft
summary: This is the third draft of a Code of Practice that sets out principles and guidelines for responsible conduct. It is intended to help stakeholders align their actions with industry best practices and regulatory expectations.

title: AI Pact Draft
summary: The AI Pact Draft proposes a collaborative framework for developing and deploying artificial intelligence responsibly, emphasizing transparency, fairness, and accountability across industry, academia, and government. It seeks to align AI systems with shared human values and mitigate risks through coordinated policy and best‑practice standards.

title: AI Pact Final
summary: The AI Pact Final sets out a shared framework for responsible AI creation and deployment, establishing guidelines to safeguard users and society. It emphasizes transparency, fairness, and safety, with commitments from stakeholders to monitor and enforce these standards.

title: Guidelines on prohibited artificial intelligence (AI) practices
summary: These guidelines identify which AI actions are not allowed, outlining behaviors and uses that are prohibited to protect safety, privacy, and fairness. They serve as a reference for organizations to ensure their AI systems comply with ethical and regulatory standards.

title: Guidelines on AI System Definition
summary: These guidelines explain what constitutes an AI system, including its components, capabilities, and the contexts in which it operates. They provide clear definitions and criteria to help organizations identify, classify, and manage AI projects effectively.

title: Communication on Boosting Start-Ups & Innovation
summary: This policy outlines how the organization will communicate to support the growth of start‑ups and foster innovation. It details strategies for internal and external messaging, collaboration with partners, and public outreach to promote new ideas and business development.

title: EuroHPC Initiative for Start-Ups
summary: The EuroHPC Initiative for Start-Ups is a European program that provides early-stage companies with access to high-performance computing resources and expertise. By offering shared infrastructure, training, and potential funding, it aims to accelerate innovation and competitiveness for start-ups across the continent.

title: Slideshow: Webinar on Risk Management
summary: This policy provides guidelines for creating and delivering a webinar slideshow focused on risk management. It includes best practices for clear communication, audience engagement, and ensuring that risk information is presented accurately and responsibly.

title: Video: Webinar on Risk Management
summary: The webinar explains how to spot potential risks in AI systems, evaluate their impact, and take steps to reduce them while staying compliant with regulations. It also covers ongoing monitoring and quick response plans to keep AI operations safe and reliable.
